4.4 Where the parties agree to vary or revoke an access agreement, they must jointly notify the CAC of the variation or revocation by e-mail at the address set out above. The notification may be given by either party on behalf of both parties. It must be in writing and dated, state that the variation or revocation is being made under the statutory right of access framework and be signed by or on behalf of both parties. If the notification relates to a variation, it must identify the terms of the existing access agreement that are to be varied and provide a copy of the access agreement containing the new terms. A proforma for this purpose can be found on the CAC’s website at www.cac.gov.uk.

Making an application to the CAC

5.1 An application may then be made to the CAC where the employer has not given a response notice before the end of the response period or where the employer has given a response notice and the negotiation period has ended without the union and the employer agreeing in writing the terms on which officials of the union are to have access. (see para 4.2 above).

5.2 An application must be made within 55 working days from the date the original access request was given. The CAC may extend that period to 70 working days where it considers that it was not reasonably practicable to apply within the 55 working day period.

5.3 The relevant form should be completed in as much detail as possible. The applicant should complete the form in the knowledge that it, and any supporting documents sent with it, will be copied to the other party. The application should therefore not contain confidential worker details, commercially sensitive material or unnecessary personal data unless the applicant is willing for that material to be copied to the other party or the CAC has specifically requested it.

5.4 When the CAC receives a right of access application, it will copy it to the other party and invite that party to provide a response. The response will in turn be copied to the applicant and to the Panel appointed to deal with the application. The Case Manager will then contact both parties to explain the course of action the Panel has decided to take.

5.5 The CAC cannot accept a right of access application unless the statutory requirements for making it have been met.

5.6 Those requirements include that a qualifying trade union has made a written and dated access request to the employer, that the employer has 21 or more workers overall, that the request contains the information required by the legislation, and that it has been given to the employer in the manner required by the legislation. This means that the request must be sent either by post, or delivered in person, to the employer’s registered office, head office or principal place of business; or sent electronically to an electronic communication address provided by the employer to the union. If the employer has not provided such an address, the request may be sent to an electronic communication address that the employer has made publicly available for communications with it.

When an application must be rejected

6.1 Following receipt of an application, the CAC must refuse access where the employer whose workers are the subject of the access request has fewer than 21 workers overall. This threshold applies to the employer as a whole and not to the group of workers to whom access is sought. The CAC must also refuse access where the proposed access agreement does not provide for at least five working days’ notice before the first instance of access takes place, or where the proposed agreement would last for more than two years unless the parties have agreed to extend it. The CAC must also refuse access where it considers it necessary in the interests of national security to do so.

When an application may be rejected

7.1 It may be reasonable for the CAC to refuse access where the workers covered by the access request are already covered by an existing recognition agreement, an ongoing statutory recognition process, or a statutory access agreement. If only some of the workers are covered by the existing arrangements or fall within the bargaining unit subject to the statutory recognition process then the CAC may still consider an access request for those workers that are not covered.

7.2 It may also be reasonable for the CAC to refuse access where more than one access request is made in respect of the same employer and at least one worker falls within scope of both requests.

Compliance and enforcement

8.1 Parties are expected to comply with any access agreement made under the statutory framework or with any CAC determination specifying access arrangements. The employer is responsible for taking reasonable steps to facilitate access, and the union is required to exercise access in a way that does not unreasonably interfere with the employer’s business. Where an agreement or determination includes conditions or safeguards, those conditions form part of the access arrangements and should be observed by the parties.

8.2 If disagreements arise about the operation of an access agreement, the parties should seek to resolve them through dialogue wherever possible. They should also make full use of any mechanism included in the access agreement to resolve such disputes. It is good practice for the employer and the union each to nominate a lead contact specifically for questions or disagreements about the implementation of access arrangements. The parties may wish to consider approaching Acas for assistance if they are unable to resolve the matter for themselves.

11.3 The procedure at the hearing is orderly but seeks to avoid unnecessary formality. Each party will be asked to comment on and amplify its written statement, to comment on the other party’s evidence and to answer questions put by the Panel. The Panel Chair may allow questions to be put to speakers or witnesses where this is necessary to deal with factual issues.

11.4 Hearings will normally be arranged as quickly as possible and will normally be completed in a day.

CAC determinations, declarations and orders

12.1 Where the CAC determines that access should take place, its determination will specify the form of access, the workers or categories of workers covered, the workplace or workplaces concerned, timing, frequency, duration, location, digital channels and any reasonable conditions or safeguards. Where the CAC deals with a complaint alleging breach of an access agreement, it may declare whether the complaint is well-founded and, where appropriate, make an order requiring specified steps to be taken. Complaints and breaches are explained further at paragraphs 8.1 to 8.7.

12.2 CAC determinations, declarations and orders are published on the CAC’s website.

Appeals

13.1 A party may appeal to the Employment Appeal Tribunal against a CAC determination or order made under the statutory right of access provisions. This includes an appeal against a penalty order made by the CAC under the enforcement provisions.

User Satisfaction

If you are asked for your views on any aspect of our service, we would appreciate your cooperation. But if you have comments, whether of satisfaction, complaint or suggestion, please do not wait to be asked. If you are dissatisfied with any aspect of our service, please let us know so that we can put things right. If you cannot resolve the problem with the person who dealt with you originally, please ask to speak to the Operations Manager or, if necessary, the Chief Executive who will investigate your complaint. If you wish to complain in writing, please send an email to enquiries@cac.gov.uk for the attention of Maverlie Tavares, Chief Executive or post it to the above address.

In the event of any complaint, we hope that you will let us try to put things right. But, if necessary, you can write to your MP who can tell you how to have your complaint referred to the Parliamentary Commissioner for Administration (the Ombudsman).
